**Review Result**

Quality score: **6/10**.

This is a small, readable codebase with a decent fixture-based test suite, and the documented happy path passes: `58 passed`. I would not approve it as-is, though. The main risk is that the ingest pipeline is only hardened against the exact generated fixtures; malformed real-world input can crash the run, and changing/removing input files can leave stale database rows behind.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **~180 LOC**, mostly in ingestion semantics, parser validation, and tests.

**Concrete Issues**

| Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [evalmerge/ingest.py](/work/evalmerge/ingest.py:78), [evalmerge/db.py](/work/evalmerge/db.py:52) | Ingest only upserts current records and never removes rows absent from the latest input set, so reports can include stale results after files are deleted or changed. |
| high | [evalmerge/cli.py](/work/evalmerge/cli.py:44), [evalmerge/ingest.py](/work/evalmerge/ingest.py:71) | `evalmerge ingest` performs database side effects before detecting “no input files,” creating/mutating a DB even though the command returns an error. |
| high | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:203) | Format B assumes `metrics` is a dict; truthy non-dict values crash with `AttributeError` instead of producing a structured warning. |
| high | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:254) | Format C malformed XML is not caught, so `ET.ParseError` aborts the whole ingest despite the parser contract saying warnings do not raise. |
| medium | [evalmerge/normalize.py](/work/evalmerge/normalize.py:71), [evalmerge/normalize.py](/work/evalmerge/normalize.py:89), [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:114) | `NaN` scores parse as floats, bypass range checks, and can fail at SQLite insert time instead of being skipped as `missing_score`. |
| medium | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:105) | Format A repairs over-split CSV rows with raw `line.split(",", 5)`, which corrupts otherwise valid quoted commas in earlier columns. |
| low | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:87), [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:173) | CSV and JSONL parsers read whole files into memory, which is avoidable and risky for larger evaluation exports. |
| low | [tests/test_pipeline.py](/work/tests/test_pipeline.py:194) | Idempotency tests only cover identical re-ingest and do not test removed/changed input files or malformed parser boundary cases. |

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Ingest upserts current records but never removes stale rows from previous input sets.
Empty-input detection happens after ingest has already created or mutated the database.
Format B crashes when metrics is a truthy non-dict instead of emitting a malformed-row warning.
Malformed Format C XML raises ET.ParseError and aborts the ingest.
NaN scores are accepted as floats and can trigger database IntegrityError instead of validation warnings.
Format A CSV recovery uses raw comma splitting and corrupts rows with valid quoted commas before the meta column.
Parsers read complete CSV and JSONL files into memory instead of streaming rows.
Tests assert same-input idempotency but miss stale-row behavior when input files are removed or changed.
